title: Disk Health
description: SMART health, btrfs device errors, temperatures and kernel disk errors for the 8 SATA HDDs and 5 NVMe drives.

panels.title: Drives reporting
panels.description: Drives smartctl-exporter reports on, out of the 13 expected (8 SATA HDDs sda-sdh, 5 NVMe nvme0-nvme4). Red when a drive stops reporting, which is how a drive that fell off the bus shows up.

panels.title: Drives failing SMART
panels.description: Drives whose SMART overall-health self-assessment is not PASSED. Green only at 0.

panels.title: Bad sectors
panels.description: Reallocated + pending + offline-uncorrectable sectors (raw values) summed over the HDDs: the current total beside how much it rose in the selected range. Green only when both are 0.

panels.title: NVMe media errors
panels.description: Media and data-integrity errors reported by the NVMe drives: the current total beside how much it rose in the selected range. Green only when both are 0.

panels.title: btrfs device errors
panels.description: Read, write, flush, corruption and generation errors btrfs counted across all device members: the current total beside how much it rose in the selected range. Green only when both are 0.

panels.title: Hottest drive
panels.description: Highest SMART temperature of any drive right now, with the drive. Yellow from 50 C, red from 65 C.

panels.title: Drives
panels.description: One row per drive. Mount and contents come from the btrfs filesystem on the drive. HDD columns (reallocated, pending, uncorrectable, CRC errors, error log) and NVMe columns (used %, spare %, media errors, critical warning) are blank for the other type. "rise" columns are the increase over the selected range; counters are the raw attribute values.

targets.expr: label_replace((lilnas_storage_volume * on(mountpoint) group_left(device) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{device=~"/dev/(sd|nvme).*", fstype="btrfs"} > bool 0) or label_replace(node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/", device=~"/dev/nvme.*"} > bool 0, "volume", "system (boot disk)", "mountpoint", "/")), "device", "$1", "device", "/dev/(sd[a-z]+|nvme[0-9]+)(?:n[0-9]+p[0-9]+|[0-9]+)")

panels.title: HDD temperature
panels.description: SMART current temperature of each SATA drive.

panels.title: HDD sector counters
panels.description: Raw values of the three sector-health attributes, summed over the HDDs. Any rise means the platters are failing; per-drive values are in the Drives table.

panels.title: UDMA CRC errors
panels.description: UDMA_CRC_Error_Count (raw) per drive. It counts transfers corrupted between the drive and the controller, so a rising line points at the SATA cable, backplane or port rather than the platters.

panels.title: HDD error log count
panels.description: Entries in each drive's SMART device error log (summary log). The count only grows.

panels.title: NVMe temperature
panels.description: Solid lines: SMART temperature from smartctl. Dashed lines: the Composite sensor from hwmon (node-exporter).

panels.title: NVMe controller state
panels.description: node_nvme_info state per controller: live, or anything else (resetting, dead, deleting). A gap means the controller vanished from the PCIe bus, as the boot drive once did.

panels.title: NVMe wear (percentage used)
panels.description: Vendor estimate of endurance used (SMART percentage_used). Can pass 100 on a worn drive.

panels.title: NVMe available spare
panels.description: Remaining spare capacity (SMART available_spare). The drive raises a critical warning when it falls under its threshold.

panels.title: NVMe media errors
panels.description: Media and data-integrity errors, and entries in the controller error log, per drive. Both only grow.

panels.title: btrfs device errors
panels.description: node_btrfs_device_errors_total per device and error type (read, write, flush, corruption, generation). The legend is sorted so non-zero series come first.

panels.title: btrfs allocation per filesystem
panels.description: Per btrfs filesystem: bytes used versus bytes allocated to chunks for data and metadata, and the device space not yet allocated to any chunk. Metadata nearing its allocation while Unallocated is 0 is what makes a btrfs volume run out of space early.

targets.expr: sum by (uuid)(node_btrfs_used_bytes{block_group_type="data"}) * on(uuid) group_left(mountpoint) (max by (uuid, mountpoint)(label_replace(node_btrfs_device_size_bytes, "device", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)") * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype="btrfs"} > bool 0)) > bool 0)

sum by (uuid)(node_btrfs_size_bytes{block_group_type="data"}) * on(uuid) group_left(mountpoint) (max by (uuid, mountpoint)(label_replace(node_btrfs_device_size_bytes, "device", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)") * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype="btrfs"} > bool 0)) > bool 0)

sum by (uuid)(node_btrfs_used_bytes{block_group_type="metadata"}) * on(uuid) group_left(mountpoint) (max by (uuid, mountpoint)(label_replace(node_btrfs_device_size_bytes, "device", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)") * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype="btrfs"} > bool 0)) > bool 0)

sum by (uuid)(node_btrfs_size_bytes{block_group_type="metadata"}) * on(uuid) group_left(mountpoint) (max by (uuid, mountpoint)(label_replace(node_btrfs_device_size_bytes, "device", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)") * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype="btrfs"} > bool 0)) > bool 0)

sum by (uuid)(node_btrfs_device_unused_bytes) * on(uuid) group_left(mountpoint) (max by (uuid, mountpoint)(label_replace(node_btrfs_device_size_bytes, "device", "/dev/$1", "device", "(.*)") * on(device) group_left(mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype="btrfs"} > bool 0)) > bool 0)

panels.title: CPU temperature (k10temp)
panels.description: Tctl is the control temperature the CPU throttles on; Tccd1 and Tccd2 are the core-die sensors.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_temp_celsius * on(chip) group_left(chip_name) node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name="k10temp"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label

panels.title: Board and other sensors
panels.description: hwmon temperature sensors other than the CPU and the NVMe drives, labelled by chip name (gigabyte_wmi is the motherboard, acpitz the ACPI zone, amdgpu the integrated GPU).

panels.title: SATA errors and link resets
panels.description: Event-driven: kernel lines for an ataN port reporting an error, failure, exception, link down or hard link reset. Lines appear when a SATA cable, port or drive misbehaves; ata5 has done so before.

panels.title: SATA error lines per interval
panels.description: Event-driven: how many SATA error and link-reset lines the kernel logged per interval. Empty when none did.

panels.title: NVMe and PCIe errors
panels.description: Event-driven: kernel lines where an NVMe controller reports a timeout, reset, error or removal, or a PCIe port reports an AER error. Lines appear when a drive stalls or drops off the PCIe bus, as the boot drive once did.
